audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers carry Gnar/Skill/Sion/Sion/Gnar/Sion/Sion. The packet and the mirror audit (gnar__sion) both give Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Gnar/Sion — and the page's own whys already argue the packet version row for row.
audit.why: whys[1] says he wins short trades at Level 2, whys[2] calls Level 3 his strongest window, whys[3] and whys[4] both say neither side has an edge, whys[5] says the ratio has not flipped at first item. The rows were simply out of order against the prose.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Gnar/Sion in both layers as one group, ratings following (Skill 5/10, Gnar 3/10, Sion 6/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why says 'Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes', while content spikes[2] and whys[5] both say first item does not flip the ratio because Boomerang Throw scales off your own HP.
audit.why: Stacking HP against percent-max-HP damage feeds the thing that hurts you; the first-item row belongs to Gnar.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why rewritten to match the Gnar-favoured first-item row.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown is named anywhere in the matchup (packet defect: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'). Hop is the single ability that defeats the whole Sion pattern and its cooldown is never given.
audit.why: Hop (E) is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12 — at rank 1 that is a 22s window with no way to leave your charged Q. Boomerang Throw is 16s at rank 1 and only refunds if he catches it. GNAR! is 90/60/30 and stuns extra on a wall, which makes standing away from walls a real positioning rule.
audit.corrected: Hop's 22s put into whys[3], the catch-refund into whys[1], GNAR!'s 90s and the wall condition into spikes[1].
